Joint Rate Comparisons

Community Power (Community Power) and San Diego Gas & Electric® (SDG&E®) have jointly
created a comparison of our typical electric rates, average monthly bills and electric generation
power sources. SDG&E implemented adjustments to its electric rates effective August 1, 2026.
Community Power updated its electric rates on May 1, 2026. The California Public Utilities
Commission requires that this comparison be posted online within 60 days of each rate
change.
To select the correct comparison to review, find the rate plan that applies to you in the chart

Need help finding your rate?
Your rate can be found in My Energy Center – www.myenergycenter.com - under the “Billing”
> “Pricing Plan” tab. It is also listed on your SDG&E bill under “Detail of Current Charges”,
directly under Electric Service.
Definition of Terms
Power Source is the mix of energy resources for generating electricity. This makes up the
electric power generation mix that is purchased or generated by your provider and delivered to
you. Your electric power may be a mix of renewable energy, natural gas and other sources.
Generation Rate is the cost of generating and/or purchasing electricity to power your home or
business. The generation rate varies based on your energy provider and the resources
included in your energy provider’s generation power source.
SDG&E Delivery Rate is SDG&E’s charge to deliver electricity to your home or business. The
electric delivery rate may vary depending on your rate and electricity use; however, it is
charged equally to customers regardless of who provides their electric generation. The delivery
rate includes the Base Services Charge (BSC), which covers investments in infrastructure, like
transformers and meters, as well as customer service to help ensure that electricity is
delivered safely and reliably to your home.
Power Charge Indifference Adjustment (PCIA) is a charge to ensure that both SDG&E
customers and those who have left SDG&E service to purchase electricity from other providers
pay the above market costs for generation resources that were procured by SDG&E on their
behalf. “Above market” refers to the difference between what the utility pays for electric
generation and current market prices for the sale of those resources.
Franchise Fees (FF) are the surcharges applied to electricity transported over SDG&E
systems that are constructed in public streets and highways. SDG&E collects the surcharge
from customers and remits them to the appropriate municipality. This is charged equally to
customers regardless of who provides their electric generation.
The unbundled Renewable Energy Credits (RECs) retired in association with Community
Power’s portfolio were produced by an eligible renewable wind resource. The resource was
built before the state’s location-based renewable energy law took effect. Community Power
received these RECs from SDG&E via a state-approved allocation process. Thus, the
unbundled RECs are not reflected in the Community Power renewable %.
